geography: Xiaoshiba Lagerstätte, Yunnan, China (early fossil evidence)
overview: A hemichordate lineage that includes living tube-dwelling pterobranchs and the graptolite radiation; fossil tubes and zooids are evaluated separately from molecular or navigation relationships.

ecology.diet: Suspension feeding in directly observed Rhabdopleura; extinct forms vary
ecology.habitat: Marine benthic colonies in living representatives, with extinct benthic and planktonic forms
ecology.locomotion: Mostly sessile zooids housed in secreted tubes
ecology.bodySize: Millimetre-scale zooids; colonies and fossil tubaria can be much larger
ecology.guild: Suspension feeder in the living species directly studied

traits: Secreted tubular housing with fusellar construction in diagnostic fossil and living graptolithines
Colonial zooids interconnected by a stolon in Yunotubus and living rhabdopleurids
Tentaculate, ciliated feeding arms in directly observed living Rhabdopleura
evidenceSummary: The 516 Ma Yunotubus colony preserves diagnostic tube construction and a stolon, while video and electron microscopy document suspension feeding in living Rhabdopleura; neither source makes every Cambrian tube a pterobranch.

overview: A Famennian total-group lamprey known from one 4.2 cm body fossil with a preserved oral disc and branchial basket.

ecology.diet: Undetermined; the oral disc does not by itself demonstrate parasitism
ecology.habitat: Waterloo Farm depositional setting; life habitat was not directly observed
ecology.locomotion: Elongate aquatic swimmer; performance was not measured

evidenceSummary: Holotype AM5750 directly records lamprey-grade anatomy, but it neither sets a crown-lamprey first appearance nor preserves lifecycle or feeding behaviour.

overview: A Moscovian cyclostome represented by a holotype and paratype whose revised anatomy combines general cyclostome and hagfish specializations.

ecology.habitat: Francis Creek Shale depositional setting; life habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Elongate aquatic swimmer; performance not measured

evidenceSummary: FMNH PF15373 and PF8472 support a stem or putative total-group hagfish interpretation, while preservation leaves several structures equivocal and excludes the fossils from the crown-Myxini range.

overview: A complete Cenomanian hagfish body fossil recovered within crown Myxini in a morphology-based phylogenetic analysis.

ecology.habitat: Marine Tethyan Lagerstätte context
ecology.locomotion: Elongate aquatic swimmer; performance not measured
ecology.bodySize: Complete body fossil; size follows the figured holotype

evidenceSummary: BHI 6445 supplies a crown-hagfish fossil bound and anatomical character set, but one specimen does not establish a global FAD, ecology or uninterrupted range.

commonNameZh: 志留纪齿旋软骨鱼干群
overview: A late Aeronian stem chondrichthyan known from twenty-three isolated tooth whorls rather than an articulated body or jaw.

ecology.diet: Undetermined; tooth whorls do not preserve feeding events
ecology.habitat: Rongxi Formation depositional setting; life habitat unresolved

evidenceSummary: IVPP V26641 and referred whorls directly record dentition and histology at about 439 Ma, but associated body anatomy, crown membership and global range remain unknown.

overview: A near-complete Telychian total-group chondrichthyan combining a scale-covered body and chondrichthyan-like branchial region with macromeric thoracic armour.

ecology.habitat: Huixingshao Formation depositional setting; life habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Aquatic body form preserved; performance not measured

evidenceSummary: The sole holotype IVPP V300000 supplies exceptional body-plan evidence while leaving exact stem placement, ecology and population variation unresolved.

commonNameZh: 泥盆纪镶嵌型软骨鱼干群
overview: A Givetian stem chondrichthyan known from one compressed specimen whose CT and histology reveal an anatomically incongruent character mosaic.

ecology.habitat: Lower Plattenkalk depositional setting; life habitat unresolved

traits: Scales and teeth preserved in one slab
evidenceSummary: UMZC 2000.32 documents multiple anatomical systems and chondrichthyan-stem placement, but compression, one individual and matrix sensitivity limit broader inference.

overview: An Eifelian early ray-finned fish represented by multiple museum specimens whose endoskeleton and scales were examined with CT.

ecology.diet: Undetermined by the cited CT study
ecology.habitat: Achanarras lake deposits; detailed niche unresolved
ecology.bodySize: Multiple partial specimens; no single profile-wide estimate

evidenceSummary: Named Scottish specimens expose an early actinopterygian anatomical mosaic; the study does not define a global first appearance, direct ancestry or detailed ecology.

overview: A Middle Triassic scanilepiform whose revised anatomy and CT-informed phylogenetic placement materially changed one estimate of the living ray-fin crown minimum.

ecology.diet: Undetermined by the cited topology studies
ecology.habitat: Kelamayi Formation depositional context; niche unresolved

traits: CT-visible endoskeletal characters used in phylogeny
evidenceSummary: IVPP V4096.6 and V4096.13 anchor the revised placement; the resulting 45-million-year calibration shift is topology-dependent rather than a direct observation of crown origin.

overview: A Kungurian articulated holotype combining frog-like and salamander-like features and recovered as a stem batrachian in the original analysis.

ecology.diet: Small-prey feeding inferred from anatomy; direct diet unavailable
ecology.habitat: Clear Fork Group depositional context; detailed niche unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial or semiaquatic performance not directly measured
ecology.guild: Inferred small predator; not directly observed

evidenceSummary: USNM 489135 is a uniquely informative individual, but its stem-batrachian placement is analysis-dependent and does not settle lissamphibian origins.

overview: An Early Triassic stem salientian known from one split-nodule holotype re-examined with micro-CT.

ecology.habitat: Sakamena-equivalent depositional context; niche unresolved
ecology.bodySize: Small holotype preserved in part and counterpart

evidenceSummary: MNHN.F.MAE.126 records a stem-salientian mosaic and hidden anatomy, while provenance, stage-scale dating and locomotor interpretation remain bounded.

overview: An Oxfordian salamandroid genus represented by one holotype and five referred articulated specimens, including material with larval structures.

ecology.habitat: Tiaojishan Formation depositional setting; niche unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Aquatic or semiaquatic inference remains specimen-dependent

evidenceSummary: PKUP V0601–V0606 support salamandroid placement and a neoteny interpretation, but the zircon age comes from overlying rock and both placement and development remain analysis-sensitive.

overview: A Norian stem gymnophionomorph represented by isolated three-dimensional bones from at least seventy-six individuals in one dated bonebed.

ecology.diet: Small-prey feeding inferred, not directly observed
ecology.habitat: Bonebed depositional context; burrowing and niche remain inferential
ecology.bodySize: Small-bodied individuals represented by isolated elements

evidenceSummary: The large disarticulated sample and U–Pb-bracketed locality support a caecilian total-group record and one dissorophoid-origin analysis without dating crown Gymnophiona or settling all lissamphibian-origin models.

overview: A once-dominant radiation of hoofed mammals represented today by horses, rhinoceroses and tapirs, together with a much richer extinct diversity.

ecology.habitat: Forest to open grassland

evidenceSummary: The group is documented by abundant Eocene-to-Recent skeletons, teeth and occurrences; relationships among some early branches remain debated.

overview: Eocene browsers that evolved rapidly from modest-bodied ancestors into rhinoceros-sized forms with distinctive skull appendages.

ecology.habitat: Woodland and forest

traits: Paired nasal or frontal appendages in some genera
evidenceSummary: Abundant skulls and skeletons establish a rapid Eocene radiation, but their exact position near the base of Perissodactyla is not fully resolved.

overview: A European palaeothere related to the horse side of perissodactyl evolution, with several species adapted to forest browsing.

ecology.habitat: Forest

evidenceSummary: Teeth and skeletons are common in European Paleogene deposits; species boundaries and locomotor interpretations vary among studies.

overview: A hornless rhinocerotoid whose short limbs, broad torso, high-set eyes and river-deposit occurrences support a semi-aquatic interpretation.

ecology.habitat: River margin and woodland

evidenceSummary: Several traits and depositional settings are consistent with semi-aquatic habits, but that inference should not be generalized to all amynodonts.

overview: One of the largest known land-mammal lineages, comprising long-limbed, long-necked hornless rhinocerotoids of Oligocene Asia.

ecology.habitat: Open woodland

evidenceSummary: Skulls, jaws and postcranial remains support its rhinocerotoid identity; phylogenetic and dispersal hypotheses continue to be revised by new Asian fossils.

overview: A genus within the more diverse chalicothere radiation; this profile does not treat every family- or subfamily-level trait as diagnostic of Chalicotherium itself.

ecology.habitat: Woodland

traits: Forelimb and feeding-posture interpretations require specimen-level attribution
evidenceSummary: Claw-bearing limbs are secure for chalicotheres, but this genus-level profile withholds family-wide branch-pulling and posture claims unless they are tied to identified Chalicotherium material.

overview: A widespread Miocene three-toed horse with low-crowned teeth suited primarily to browsing rather than dedicated grazing.

ecology.habitat: Forest and woodland

evidenceSummary: Dental crown height and wear support browsing, while occurrences document dispersal from North America into Eurasia.

regionalRanges.label: North American tribe-level range
regionalRanges.basis: The North American hipparionin radiation begins near 17 Ma and the classic four-genus synthesis extends to about 2 Ma; exact endpoints remain pending a revised genus-level synthesis.

regionalRanges.label: Old World first dispersal
regionalRanges.basis: The oldest well-supported Old World dispersal window is represented by early Hippotherium records in the Vienna Basin.

regionalRanges.label: Latest Old World regional records
regionalRanges.basis: Terminal records vary by lineage and region; the review places the latest Chinese and African hipparionins around or below 1 Ma rather than at the Holocene boundary.

overview: A tribe of tridactyl horses that diversified across the Old and New Worlds; this entity avoids treating the genus Hipparion sensu stricto as the entire radiation.

ecology.habitat: Open woodland and grassland

evidenceSummary: Abundant teeth and limb bones document wide ecological variation. Hipparionini is used here deliberately because historical broad use of Hipparion obscures distinct genera such as Cormohipparion and Neohipparion.

overview: A short-legged, barrel-bodied rhinoceros whose aquatic ecology is contested: Florida isotopes favor principally terrestrial populations, while multi-isotope evidence supports semi-aquatic T. major at Ashfall.

ecology.habitat: Open habitats, wetlands and river-adjacent plains; locality dependent
ecology.guild: Bulk grazer or wet-habitat mixed feeder

evidenceSummary: Body shape alone is insufficient to infer behavior. Florida and Ashfall isotope studies reach different ecological conclusions, so behavior is represented as species-, locality- and time-dependent.

overview: A cold-adapted Pleistocene rhinoceros of Eurasian steppe-tundra, known from skeletons, soft-tissue remains and prehistoric art.

ecology.habitat: Cold steppe-tundra

evidenceSummary: Morphology supports cold adaptation and grazing. The display LAD is a global synthesis, distinct from regional fossil dates and from a 14.4 ka genomic sample that shows no obvious pre-extinction genomic erosion.

geography: Late Jurassic lithographic limestones of Bavaria, Germany
overview: A Late Jurassic avialan known from a small Bavarian specimen series; it lies outside crown Neornithes and is not presented as the direct ancestor of living birds.

ecology.diet: Not resolved by the cited flight and systematic studies
ecology.habitat: Solnhofen-archipelago carbonate environments represented by Bavarian lithographic limestones
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial and aerial capacities; flight style is inferred from bone geometry rather than observed behaviour
ecology.guild: Unresolved; no single feeding guild is assigned from the cited evidence

traits: Asymmetrical flight feathers associated with skeletal specimens
Toothed jaws and a long bony tail
Pectoral geometry compatible with short-burst active flight in a biomechanical comparison
evidenceSummary: The oldest referred specimen extends the genus into the earliest Tithonian Painten Formation and documents substantial anatomical variation; synchrotron comparisons support active flight capacity but not modern crown-bird flight performance.

geography: Antarctica and Europe for the two Maastrichtian fossil tests highlighted here
overview: The crown group defined by the common ancestor of living birds and all descendants; this boundary excludes Archaeopteryx and keeps Cretaceous fossil membership tied to explicit phylogenetic analyses.

ecology.diet: Highly diverse; the highlighted Vegavis skull supports underwater prey capture for that fossil only
ecology.habitat: Global across marine, freshwater and terrestrial environments today
ecology.locomotion: Predominantly volant, with multiple independently flight-reduced or flightless lineages

traits: Crown membership is defined relationally, not by one universally diagnostic fossil character
Vegavis skull anatomy combines an avian beak and crown-like neuroanatomy with a specialized feeding apparatus
Asteriornis preserves a different late Maastrichtian galloanseran character combination
evidenceSummary: A 2025 skull analysis strengthens crown-waterfowl placement for older Vegavis, but the study explicitly records its earlier contested placements; younger Asteriornis also shifts among near-crown positions under different analyses.

geography: Hell Creek, Lance and age-equivalent latest Maastrichtian formations
overview: A latest Maastrichtian tyrannosaurid represented by a large specimen sample; the dossier separates specimen anatomy and traces from fitted growth, bite-force and abundance models.

ecology.diet: Carnivorous, with direct bite-trace and coprolite evidence for bone consumption
ecology.habitat: Continental floodplain systems in western North America
ecology.bodySize: Large-bodied; size and mass estimates vary among specimens and reconstructions
ecology.guild: Large terrestrial predator and carcass processor

traits: Deep, robust skull with enlarged teeth
Ontogenetic cranial changes documented across a multi-institution specimen series
evidenceSummary: Stratigraphic census, growth-series anatomy, bone traces and coprolite contents are observations; population density, maturity, body mass, bite force and tooth pressure remain model-dependent inferences.
